speaker: howard_wolowitz
text: Which brings us to tenth grade.

speaker: penny
text: Howard, do you think maybe sometimes you try too hard?

speaker: howard_wolowitz
text: Look at me. What chance do I have if I don't try too hard?

speaker: penny
text: Well, you'd have a terrific chance. I mean, you're smart, you're funny, you have a cool job. You build stuff that goes into outer space.

speaker: penny
text: Look, I'm telling you, I've known you for, like, a year and a half and this is the first time I feel like I'm talking to a real person. And you know what? I like him, he's a nice guy.

speaker: howard_wolowitz
text: You really think so? I don't know.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Nice little bot you've got here.

speaker: barry_kripke
text: Yep. At 3400 RPM. It can cut through steel like it was wubber.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Neat. Good work. Sheldon, we've got to call this off.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: No, Leonard. For years, merciless thugs like Kripke have made my life a series of painful noogies and humiliating wedgies and the insensitively named Indian burns. That stops now.

speaker: raj_koothrappali
text: But, Sheldon, we don't have a chance. The only improvement you were able to make on the robot was to put fresh batteries in the remote.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: What you fail to realize is Kripke suffers from a fatal flaw, overconfidence from his robot's massive size and its overwhelming power.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Trust me, Kripke will fall easy prey to my psychological warfare. Observe. Kripke! I would ask if your robot is prepared to meet its maker, but as you are its maker, clearly the two of you have met.
